items.headline: Chip stocks crushed: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falls 7.2% on Friday as the AI trade enters a 'show me' phase
items.why: A 7% one-day drop in the sector that has led the market means investors are now demanding proof that AI spending earns a return, which pressures every stock priced on that growth.

items.headline: Intel plunges 28.6%, its worst day since 1974, after a fourth-quarter profit forecast missed expectations
items.why: A beat on the latest quarter was ignored because guidance disappointed, showing the market is now pricing the next quarter, not the last one.

items.headline: Alphabet had its worst day on record (down more than 12% Thursday) on higher cash burn; Amazon's trailing free cash flow is negative $42.4 billion
items.why: Two of the largest AI spenders were punished for capital spending that is outrunning cash generation, a direct challenge to the assumption that the buildout pays for itself.

items.headline: The world's largest crypto exchange suffers a hack affecting more than $6 billion; Bitcoin drops below $77,000 from above $86,000 earlier in October
items.why: A breach of this size at the top venue is a counterparty-risk shock for the whole market, and a US blockchain intelligence firm attributing it to a North Korean unit adds a sanctions angle.

items.headline: Ether ETFs bleed: outflows on 17 of October's 20 trading days (about $1.35 billion), while spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $137 million Wednesday
items.why: Institutional demand is diverging, with Bitcoin still attracting inflows while Ether sees its second-largest monthly outflow on record, and Bitcoin is trading with the Nasdaq-100 (30-day correlation 0.64) rather than as a haven.

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75%-4.00% on October 28 after September's first hike since 2023; two officials dissented in favour of another hike
items.why: With markets pricing roughly an 80% chance of a December hike, the debate has shifted from when to cut to whether to tighten further, which weighs on valuations of long-duration assets.

sources.title: Fed Leaves Rates Unchanged at 3.75%-4% Following October 28 FOMC Meeting

items.headline: US data stays hot: Q3 GDP grew 3.4%, core PCE rose 0.3% on the month and jobless claims fell to 194,000
items.why: Strong growth with sticky inflation gives the Fed cover to keep tightening, so good economic news is currently bad news for rate-sensitive markets.

items.headline: Treasury yields stay elevated: 10-year 4.94%, 30-year 5.31%, 2-year 4.56% at Friday's close
items.why: A 5%-plus long bond raises the hurdle rate for equities and is the stated concern behind worries that data-center construction will slow.

items.headline: Gold falls 3.3% to $3,898.90, a one-year low; silver drops 5.9% to $49.14, below $50 for the first time in 11 months
items.why: Metals are being sold as rate-hike odds rise, a reminder that non-yielding assets lose when real yields climb, even with a war premium in oil.

items.headline: Brent settles up 2.4% at $113.43 and WTI at $104.12 with the Middle East conflict ongoing; energy is the only strong sector
items.why: Oil above $100 keeps inflation and rate-hike pressure alive, and energy stocks (+1.9% Friday) are the one place absorbing money leaving tech.

items.headline: S&P 500 closes at 7,580.07 (-1.8%), off an intraday low of 7,527.67, about 3.1% below its record, for a third straight weekly loss
items.why: The 7,527 intraday low is now the level to watch: a close below it would confirm the pullback is deepening beyond a one-day shakeout.

items.headline: Narrow, tech-led damage: Nasdaq-100 -3.5% and technology sector -4.9%, while the equal-weight S&P 500 fell only 0.8% and energy gained 1.9%
items.why: The gap between the cap-weighted and equal-weight index shows the selling is concentrated in AI leaders, not a broad market break.

items.headline: Bitcoin loses the $79,000-$80,000 demand zone and trades below $77,000
items.why: That zone was the support cited earlier in the week with $82,000 as the first reclaim target; with it broken, former support becomes resistance.

items.why: All three published supports gave way in a single session, so $4,000 flips to resistance for now.
